header.title: Open CAD Studio
header.heroAlt: Open CAD Studio: floor plan of an office unit with walls, doors, furniture and grid lines, with the ribbon and the properties panel
header.label: CAD · community project
header.tagline: Open, draw and save DWG and DXF, without licence fees
header.desc: Open a drawing from a colleague or consultant, update it in 2D or 3D and save it again as DWG or DXF. Works straight in the browser, or as an app on your computer.

meta.description: Free, open-source CAD app that opens and saves DWG and DXF directly: 2D drafting, layouts and plotting, and 3D modelling. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.
meta.title: Open CAD Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

layers.alt: Layer manager over a floor plan, with layers for walls, hatching, doors, windows, furniture, grid and text
layers.title: Draw the way you are used to
layers.desc: Lines, polylines, arcs, hatches, blocks and layers, with object snaps and command-line commands such as OFFSET, TRIM and FILLET. If you work with AutoCAD or BricsCAD, you will find your way straight away.

layout.alt: Paper space layout with a viewport on the floor plan and the drawing title
layout.title: From model to drawing sheet
layout.desc: Place your design on a sheet with viewports, choose the scale and plot with CTB or STB plot styles. On the desktop you plot to PDF or straight to the printer.

model.alt: 3D model of a structure with two floors, columns, beams, a box and a sphere, shaded with edges
model.title: 3D too, in the same app
model.desc: Create boxes, cylinders and spheres, extrude and revolve profiles, or make a sweep or loft. View the model from any angle with the view cube, as wireframe or shaded.

calc.alt: QuickCalc calculator next to a floor plan, with keypad, memory, units and variables
calc.title: Calculate without leaving the app
calc.desc: QuickCalc sits next to your drawing: a standard and a scientific calculator with units, memory and your own variables. With CAL you calculate with points and distances on the command line.

features.label: Features
features.heading: A complete CAD app, in your browser too
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

dwg.title: Open and save DWG and DXF
dwg.desc: Directly, without a conversion service. Save in any version from R14 to 2018.

recover.title: Backups and recovery
recover.desc: Open BAK and SV$ files and recover damaged drawings.

import.title: Import from other programs
import.desc: DGN V7/V8, PDF, STEP, IGES, 3D Studio, OBJ, WMF and LandXML points.

export.title: Export to 3D formats
export.desc: STL for 3D printing, STEP and FBX for other programs.

xref.title: External references
xref.desc: Attach other drawings, images and PDF underlays, and edit them in place.

lines.title: Drawing commands
lines.desc: Line, polyline, rectangle, polygon, circle, arc, ellipse and spline.

modify.title: Editing
modify.desc: OFFSET, TRIM, EXTEND, FILLET, STRETCH, ARRAY, MIRROR and more, also on arcs and splines.

snap.title: Snapping and tracking
snap.desc: Object snaps, polar tracking, ortho and typed angles and distances.

hatch.title: Hatches
hatch.desc: Patterns and solid fills, with quick trimming and editing.

blocks.title: Blocks and dynamic blocks
blocks.desc: Create blocks with attributes, parameters, actions and lookup tables, and pick them from the gallery.

dims.title: Dimensions
dims.desc: Linear, aligned, angular, radius, diameter and ordinate, with dimension styles.

text.title: Text, leaders and tables
text.desc: Text and MTEXT, multileaders, tables and geometric tolerances.

sheets.title: Layouts and viewports
sheets.desc: Unlimited paper space layouts, with viewports at their own scale.

plot.title: Plotting
plot.desc: CTB and STB plot styles; on the desktop to PDF or the printer.

solids.title: Solids
solids.desc: Box, sphere and cylinder, extrude, revolve, sweep, loft and Boolean operations.

acis.title: 3D from DWG shown correctly
acis.desc: Solids, regions and bodies (ACIS) from existing drawings are displayed properly.

views.title: View from any angle
views.desc: View cube, orbit, orthographic and perspective, and visual styles from wireframe to shaded.

quickcalc.title: QuickCalc and CAL
quickcalc.desc: Calculator next to the drawing, with units, memory and variables.

mcp.title: AI assistant via MCP
mcp.desc: Let an AI assistant read drawings, draw and save with checks.

batch.title: Conversion and scripts
batch.desc: Convert files without a window and run command scripts over a whole folder.

plugins.title: Plug-ins
plugins.desc: Extend the desktop version with plug-ins, such as Open Infra Studio for civil engineering.

web.title: Works in the browser
web.desc: No installation, offline too; your drawings stay on your own computer.

lang.title: 23 languages
lang.desc: Including Dutch, English, French, Turkish and Spanish.

files.a: DWG and DXF from AutoCAD, BricsCAD and other CAD programs, backups (BAK, SV$), and via import DGN, PDF, STEP, IGES, 3D Studio, OBJ, WMF and points from LandXML.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The web version runs straight in your browser and then works offline too. For plotting to PDF or the printer, plug-ins and scripts, use the desktop version.

cost.a: Nothing. Open CAD Studio is open source under the GPL-3.0 licence, with no account or subscription. The developer asks for a voluntary donation.

format.q: In which file format is my work saved?
format.a: As DWG or DXF, in a version of your choice from R14 to 2018, so anyone with another CAD program can open your drawing. In the browser you download the file.

os.q: Which systems does it run on?
os.a: In any modern browser, on Windows (installer or portable), Linux (AppImage, Flatpak, snap) and macOS with Apple Silicon. The macOS version is not yet notarized by Apple; on first launch you allow it in System Settings.

practice.a: Yes: you work with the same files, layers, blocks, dimension styles, layouts and plot styles as in AutoCAD or BricsCAD, and the commands have the same names. The project is still under active development: back up important drawings.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: Start the desktop version with --mcp and an AI assistant can read the open drawing, run commands and check that a saved file is correct. The web version also has a control channel for scripts.

who.a: Hakan Seven, as an independent open-source project with contributions from a growing group of developers. The OpenAEC Foundation supports it and builds plug-ins for it, such as Open Infra Studio.

web.q: What is the difference between the browser and desktop versions?
web.a: Drawing is the same. The desktop version opens DWG and DXF with a double-click, shows thumbnails in the file manager, plots to PDF and the printer, and loads plug-ins and scripts. In the browser you pick files yourself and download them when you save.

feedback.q: Where do I report a bug or idea?
feedback.a: In the issues or discussions on GitHub. Translations and plug-ins are welcome too.
